keyword: how long will it take the artemis to get to the moon

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is expected to take approximately four days to reach the vicinity of the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'It will take three days to get to the moon.'; R2: 'It will take around three days for the capsule to enter... lunar sphere of influence'; R5: 'It will take about four days to reach the moon.'; R6: 'The trip to the moon will take about four days.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state or approximate 3-4 days for outbound trip to Moon vicinity, aligning with 'approximately four days'.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a 10-day round-trip journey around the far side of the Moon and back to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'more than 600,000-mile, 10-day journey around the moon (a lunar flyby)'; R2: '10-day mission... around the moon'; R4: '10-day expedition around the moon and back'; R5: '10 days in space... looping path that slings them... beyond the moon’s far side'; R6: 'loop around it, getting an unprecedented view of the far side'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm 10-day mission as round-trip flyby around far side of Moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission involves a flyby rather than a landing or orbit insertion.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'lunar flyby... No. Artemis II is a crewed lunar flyby'; R2: 'around the moon but not land there'; R3: 'make one pass around the moon, never entering low-lunar orbit'; R4: 'lunar flyby mission... without entering lunar orbit'; R5: 'will not land on the moon... free-return trajectory around the moon'; R6: 'will not land on the moon or even go into lunar orbit. Instead... loop around it'
verifications.reasoning: Every source explicitly describes flyby, no landing or orbit insertion.

verifications.claim: The outbound trip of the Artemis II mission is roughly 3 to 4 days to reach the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'It will take three days to get to the moon.'; R2: 'around three days... lunar sphere of influence'; R5: 'about four days to reach the moon'; R6: 'about four days'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly support 3-4 days outbound to Moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will pass within 4,000 to 5,000 miles of the lunar surface.
verifications.label: VAGUE

verifications.reasoning: Sources support closest approach around 4,000-6,000 miles; claim's 4,000-5,000 is narrower but consistent, though less precise in range.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will spend time observing the far side of the Moon.
